hypothesis: Per-user rank transform for blending instead of global rank
why: The metric only sees within-user order, so blending in per-user rank space should stop one model's global score distribution from distorting another's per-user ordering

hypothesis: Feature-statistics freshness is worth more than statistics volume
why: Test rows sit 7-17 days after the train window, so their aggregate features are stale. Before considering any rule-risky use of the validation window, measure what freshness is actually worth — using train+valid data only
change: official_lgbm.py --stats LO,HI (override the aggregate source pool) + scripts/official_staleness.py. Controlled comparison at constant 7-day window length: A = stats 04/15-04/21 (gap 0 to valid), B = stats 04/08-04/14 (gap 7)
metrics_note: DECISIVE NEGATIVE: A 0.6066 vs B 0.6069 -> freshness worth -0.0003 (noise). Window LENGTH is what matters (7d 0.6066 vs 14d 0.6080 = +0.0014). Conclusion: extending the statistics pool into the validation window could buy at most ~+0.0005 by volume, which does not justify the rules risk under FAQ 2.9.2 ('training data is the train split only'). NOT DONE. Side benefit: confirms the train-test temporal gap is not a generalization threat

what: log_random_4_22_to_5_08_pure.csv as a debiasing / propensity source
finding: Measured to be exactly co-extensive with the valid+test window (04/22-05/08, is_rand=1 throughout) with zero randomized rows inside the training window. Any per-item quantity derived from its labels would be feature statistics computed over evaluation-window labels — a hard violation of FAQ 2.9.2/2.9.3. NOT USED anywhere in this pipeline, for training or features.
also: KuaiRand-Pure has no impression-position column, so LightGBM's additive position-bias debiasing would require a fabricated proxy position; published real-log evidence (Baidu-ULTR) reports marginal improvements at most. Not pursued.

why: Ran 3.1 CPU-hours without reaching its early-stopping point on 1.1M rows with ~20 high-cardinality categoricals under ordered target statistics, while starving a correctness-check job. Terminated on resource grounds: adversarial verification of the library-diversity literature refuted every claim of blend gain from swapping GBDT libraries (0-3), so expected value did not justify the compute. Script is kept in the repo, unused by the submission.

reason: Converged under the declared rule (epsilon=0.0005, N=4): the best validation primary over the last 4 scored iterations (0.6081) exceeds the best from before that window (0.6081) by 0.0000 <= epsilon. Every hypothesis tested after the convergence point was also scored and logged, and none beat 0.6081, so the designation never changed.

resource_use.llm_tokens_estimate: ~18M total across the whole run: main agent ~2M, plus workflow subagents (3 tuning sweeps ~0.5M, two deep-research rounds ~10.2M over 206 subagents). Estimated from harness telemetry; exact per-call accounting is not exported.
resource_use.training_compute: 8-core CPU only, no GPU. Largest single training ~3.7 min; one abandoned CatBoost job consumed 3.1 CPU-hours and was terminated, see the 'abandoned' event.

human_interventions_detail: goal-level user directives only: (1) status query; (2) 'optimize to the best'; (3) 'check the official standard online / is this too little optimization'; (4) 'do it' authorizing pursuit of the freshness question; (5) request for the demo-video script. Zero manual code, feature, or hyperparameter edits by a human. Directive (4) authorized investigating a rules-gray-area technique; the agent built the measurement, found the technique worth at most +0.0005, and declined it on its own rather than taking the compliance risk.
post_convergence_note: The final exploration round tested 8 further hypotheses (sequence model as blend member and as feature, metric-aware weighting, per-user rank blending, statistics freshness, multi-lambda EASE, feature selection, CatBoost diversity). All 8 were negative or neutral; all are logged. The plateau is real, not unexplored.
